title: Affine-line and weight conventions
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], with $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne \operatorname{char}(k_0)$, and $\iota:\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\simeq\mathbf C$. Write
$A_0=\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$, $A=A_0\otimes k$, and use a prime to denote the
dual affine line. The affine-space construction is [def-sbc-affine-space]; the standard projective-line chart is [def-sc-p1-standard]. All cohomology is geometric, in the sense of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], with geometric Frobenius
([def-weil-frobenius-detailed]).
Weil sheaves mean [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], and lisse means [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. A lisse Weil sheaf is *pure of weight $w$* if every eigenvalue
$\alpha$ at a closed point $x$ satisfies
$|\iota\alpha|=q_x^{w/2}$; replace equality by $\leq$ for a punctual upper bound
([def-weil-punctual-weights]).
Use the twist construction [def-wf-tate-twist]; its weight shift is the specialization $n=-1$ of [lem-tw-tate-twist-weight-shift], so $(-1)$ raises weights by two.
A Weil sheaf $F$ is *irreducible lisse* (an *irreducible lisse Weil
sheaf*) if it is lisse and nonzero and every lisse Weil subsheaf of $F$
is $0$ or $F$: it is a simple object of the category of lisse Weil
sheaves. On a connected normal scheme such as a dense open of $A_0$, this
says that the Weil group acts irreducibly on the geometric generic stalk, by the exact fibre equivalence [cor-galois-lisse-representations] with the Weil structure [def-wf-fundamental-representation]; for curves the matching of subobjects is explicitly [prop-wf-weil-sheaf-representation-equivalence].
It is weaker than simplicity in the category of all Weil sheaves, which
never holds for a nonzero lisse sheaf on a curve: choose a closed point $x$ in a component on which its rank is positive;
the extension by zero of the restriction to the complement of $x$ is a
nonzero proper subsheaf (its stalk at $x$ is zero and its generic stalk equals that of $F$); the canonical inclusion is the counit of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction], with stalks given by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks], so it is injective by [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-detect-mono]. These constructions use [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] at each finite adic coefficient stage and then pass to the rational coefficients.

For a dense open $j:U_0\hookrightarrow A_0$, $j_*F$ denotes the
*ordinary* sheaf direct image. Its stalks at missing points are
inertia invariants by [lem-wf-boundary-stalk-invariants]; its curve perverse intermediate extension, characterized by the absence of boundary perverse subobjects and quotients, is
$j_{!*}(F[1])=(j_*F)[1]$ ([lem-dl-a1-curve-intermediate-extension], with ordinary direct image as in [def-wf-middle-extension]). A lisse Weil sheaf $F$ on $U_0$ is *unramified at infinity* if it
extends to a lisse Weil sheaf on the open $U_0\cup\{\infty\}$ of
$\mathbf P^1_{k_0}$ (with $A_0\subset\mathbf P^1_{k_0}$ the standard chart);
by [lem-dl-a1-lisse-extension-inertia] applied to $C_0=U_0\cup\{\infty\}$, this is equivalent to the condition that inertia
at $\infty\in\mathbf P^1_k$ acts trivially on the geometric generic fiber.
A Weil sheaf on $U_0$ is *geometrically constant* if its underlying étale
sheaf is constant on every connected open of $U=U_0\otimes k$; for $U$
connected this means that the geometric fundamental group acts
trivially, while its Frobenius module may be nontrivial. This last description uses [cor-galois-lisse-representations], which sends the constant sheaf to the trivial representation. Here constant means isomorphic to a finite direct sum of the constant coefficient sheaf in the adic convention, and the geometric fundamental representation and its Weil extension are those of [def-wf-fundamental-representation].

split_report.summary: Audited the definition clause by clause against main-20261015 and the slopmaster2 predicates. Exposed the finite-field, adic lisse/Weil, affine/projective-line, cohomology, and representation notions; reused existing theorem nodes for Tate weights, boundary stalks, and the lisse representation equivalence. Added two statement-only supporting results for the non-definitional lisse-extension/inertia and perverse-intermediate-extension comparisons; no new definitions and no theorem proof is hidden in the definition. Clarified that the displayed eigenvalue inequality is a punctual upper bound, not a definition of a mixed weight filtration.

The unit has no proof steps; this is a definition item rather than its separately imported sk key node.

It makes two precisions and drops nothing: 'punctual upper bound' instead of 'upper bound', so it is not confused with the filtration-based mixed bound of def-weil-punctual-weights; and the nonsimplicity remark now takes x in a component of positive rank, because the source's version fails where the rank is 0. The twist claim is n=-1 of lem-tw-tate-twist-weight-shift (w-2n). The extension-by-zero counit, stalk and mono-detection lemmas say what the remark uses. New node lem-dl-a1-lisse-extension-inertia is true. Stacks 0BTD (pione-lemma-normal-pione-quotient-inertia, checked in pione.tex l.2984) makes ker(pi1 U -> pi1 C) normally generated by boundary inertia. The other geometric points over s give W(U_0)-conjugates of I_s, so the Weil structure covers them. Uniqueness and descent come from full faithfulness of restriction. Its hypotheses match d-real-setup/d-real-boundary. Tested on S_0 empty, F=0, constant sheaves, Kummer on G_m (does not extend) and Artin-Schreier at infinity. New node lem-dl-a1-curve-intermediate-extension is true: j_{!*}=tau_{<=-1}Rj_*(F[1])=(j_*F)[1]. i^!j_*F sits in degrees >=2 and Hom(i^*j_*F,E[-1])=0, so there are no Z-supported subobjects or quotients. Tested on j=id, F=0, a punctual summand and the Kummer IC complex. Neither node duplicates an existing one: thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart clause 4 gives perversity only, lem-wf-dense-open-pi1-surjective and lem-a1-lisse-middle-extension start from sheaves already lisse on C, and lem-wf-boundary-stalk-invariants gives a stalk only. Neither restates a proof clause; they are claims moved out of a definition. No cycle, no SGA, no tool_uses. Batch-5 citations, all accepted as general notions or tools outside both assumptions: def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves, def-wf-middle-extension, d-real-boundary and def-wf-fundamental-representation are definitions, and def-wf-middle-extension already reached the PD chapter through the original blueprint uses. cor-galois-lisse-representations is the general lisse-sheaf/pi1 equivalence in the foundations unit sk-lem-finite, cited by 31 nodes, and Poincare duality neither states nor gives it. prop-wf-weil-sheaf-representation-equivalence, lem-tw-tate-twist-weight-shift and lem-wf-boundary-stalk-invariants are purity-chapter tools that reach the PD chapter only through definitions or nodes already in the item's original uses.
